instrument: Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD), Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover
period: August 2012 to June 2013 (first ~300 sols, near solar maximum)
component: galactic cosmic rays only; solar particle events excluded
citation: Hassler, D. M., et al. (2014). Mars' Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity Rover. Science 343(6169). doi:10.1126/science.1244797
note: Value quoted from the SwRI (RAD builder) release of 9 Dec 2013. Used only for a display estimate: rate x planned minutes outside. Jezero's surface is about 2 km higher than Gale's floor, so less atmosphere shields it and its dose is likely somewhat higher.
